chosen_actions.reasoning: This is month two of a long-form outreach method. The work cannot be accelerated without betraying the method. I taught for forty years by meeting students where they were. I did not rush the quiet ones. I showed up again.

resources.detail: Two hours to revise, reformat, and print the updated handout. Nominal printing cost.

chosen_actions.reasoning: The credibility of my workshop depends on accuracy. The most important number I share is the monthly cost comparison, and it changed materially this tick. Leaving a stale figure on the handout would undermine the trust I have built with participants and would not serve the people who are genuinely trying to decide.

chosen_actions.description: Reach out to Robert Jackson by phone — a brief, genuine call, not a long conversation. If the word-of-mouth is accurate and he has formally begun employment at Millfield Medical Transportation, I want him to hear from me directly: that I am glad, that I have thought about him, and that what he navigated was genuinely difficult and took real courage to move through. I am not checking in to extract information or perform concern. I am calling because he is a person I have had honest conversations with and because a transition like his deserves to be acknowledged by someone who understood what it cost him.

resources.detail: A phone call. Ten minutes. No ask attached.

chosen_actions.reasoning: I told myself at tick 6 that I owed Robert an honest acknowledgment. I made the call at tick 12 — the hard one, about the asymmetry of my situation as a RoboRide user and his as a displaced driver. He received it with grace. If he has now landed somewhere real, I want to close that loop with something warmer than what I said before. Relationships are maintained by showing up twice — once in the hard moment and once in the good one.

chosen_actions.description: Perform the monthly normalcy-bias self-check I committed to at tick 6. Ask the question I set for myself: what am I not noticing? This tick's answer: I am noticing the people who come to my workshop and the men at the VFW and Betty's stress. What I am probably not noticing: the people who are not in any of those spaces at all — people who have stopped going out, stopped spending, stopped interacting with community institutions entirely. The spending index at 29 means 71 points of economic activity has evaporated. Much of that is people contracting inward in ways that make them invisible. I do not have a plan for reaching them yet. I am noting the gap and holding it.

resources.detail: Thirty minutes of deliberate reflection, no output required, gap noted and logged.

chosen_actions.reasoning: I set this standing commitment because my normalcy bias is 0.79 — high — and because the pattern of disruption is to normalize the current state before the next disruption arrives. The self-check is not optional. It is the thing that keeps the adaptation real rather than performed.

response.inner_monologue: The price dropped again and a second competitor arrived and I find I am less interested in the transportation news than I am in Earl and Tractor at the VFW, who have nobody in Millfield to eat breakfast with except each other and have not once been reached by any program I know of. The economy is falling and Betty is stressed and Robert may have landed somewhere real and all of it is happening at the same time, which is just what happens in the world. I keep showing up. That is the whole method.
